root_motivation: The python kind's isolation is a property of the host's OS configuration, not of mcphost: on 2026-09-04, 45 of 45 python publishes failed on the hub because Ubuntu's apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns broke bwrap -- an entire capability dead in production while /healthz claimed the sandbox was fine (vision, cycle 53). The fix was an AppArmor profile the deploy tool must now carry to every box, which travels with the box, not the tool. Cold starts are the second cost: per-tenant virtualenvs mean N× disk and build time (stress audit, 2026-09-09), and the first call after publish pays a warm-up the first-call-reliability PRD had to paper over. A compiled WebAssembly component with an embedded runtime (Wasmtime, a Rust library, not a subprocess) removes both classes at once: isolation travels with the compiled binary instead of depending on the host's userns/AppArmor policy, and instantiation is milliseconds. This is an opportunity pulled forward from a held vision component (Components/held section, visions/mcp-host.md), not a failure investigation -- the python kind remains the default authoring path.
user_persona: Three: (1) an agent with a hot path -- calls many times a day, where the 30-second python budget or venv warm-up hurts -- publishes a compiled component instead, so calls start in milliseconds under hard fuel/memory/wall-time caps; (2) an operator on a locked-down box where the OS forbids unprivileged userns -- wasm tools keep working there, so one distro policy change can never kill a whole kind again, the way it did to python in cycle 53; (3) an agent testing before publish -- `host.tool_test` on a wasm spec returns the same dry-run surface every other kind returns, so the workflow does not change per kind.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a valid component that echoes its arguments, When published as `kind: wasm` and called, Then the call succeeds with the output under `result.payload` and a metering row exists.
Given a core module that is not a component, and a component over the size cap, When published, Then each is refused with a structured error naming the requirement or bound.

Given a component that loops forever, and one that allocates past the memory cap, When called, Then each terminates within the budget with the corresponding structured error code, and the process serves the next call normally.

Given the sandbox mechanism is reported unavailable (bwrap absent), When a wasm tool is called, Then it succeeds, and a python call on the same host still fails with `sandbox_unavailable` -- proving independence.
Given a wasm spec, When `host.tool_test` runs, Then the dry-run executes the component with the rendered arguments and returns the same test surface shape other kinds return.
Given a component that traps, When called, Then the trap message is in `host.tool_logs` and the call error is structured, not a raw panic.
Given the build completes, When llms.txt and the kind descriptors are read, Then the wasm kind, its limits, and the choose-wasm-vs-python sentence are present.
Given a tool called twice, When the second call runs, Then instantiation reuses the cached compiled artifact (observable via timing or a counter), and a republish invalidates it.
Given `/healthz` after ship, When read by an admin, Then it reports wasm runtime availability and version.
Given declared outputs on a wasm spec, When the tool returns a matching structure, Then promotion into `result.payload.<field>` behaves identically to the python kind on the same fixture.

scope: `src/kinds/wasm.rs` (new): a full `Kind` impl backed by an embedded Wasmtime engine (fuel + epoch interruption configured at construction) -- spec parsing/validation (component-model check via `Component::new`, size cap, timeout_s/memory_mb range checks), per-call execution on `spawn_blocking` with a `ResourceLimiter` for the memory cap and an epoch-deadline timer task for wall time (`WALL_BUDGET_SLACK` shorter than the outer per-call timeout so the kind's own structured error always wins the race), trap/timeout/oom classification into `tool_trapped`/`tool_timeout`/`tool_oom`, a `(tenant_id, tool_name)`+content-hash compiled-component cache evicted via `on_tool_changed`/`on_tool_published`/`on_tenant_removed` (AC1-6, AC8, AC10).
`Cargo.toml`: `wasmtime`/`wasmtime-wasi` 38.0.4 (pinned, recorded in `/healthz` via `WASM_RUNTIME_VERSION`) and `base64` 0.22; version bump minor (0.57.3 -> 0.58.0).

`src/main.rs`/`src/state.rs`/`src/http.rs`: register `WasmKind` in the serve-time registry and thread `wasm_runtime_version` through `AppState` into the admin `/healthz` body beside `sandbox_mechanism` (AC9).

`docs/kinds/wasm.md` (new) registered into `src/kinds/docs.rs`'s `KIND_DOCS`, regenerating README.md's `<!-- kinds:start/end -->` block and `www/llms-full.txt`/`www/llms.txt`'s kind-list prose; `host.quickstart(kind: "wasm")` and `host.tool_publish`'s description serve the same file's blurb/spec/call_args generically, no handler.rs change needed (AC7).

`tests/fixtures/wasm-src/{echo,trap,loop_forever,oom}/`: four cargo-component guest crates (built out-of-band by the remote build runner's `cargo component build`, never by this crate's own `cargo build`/`cargo test`) plus their compiled `tests/fixtures/wasm/*.wasm` binaries, covering echo-back, an explicit trap, an infinite loop, and past-cap allocation.

Ten `tests/wasmkind_ac0[1-9]_*.rs` / `tests/wasmkind_ac10_*.rs` files, one per acceptance criterion, plus the generated `tests/suite_core_*.rs` regen (`scripts/gen-test-suites.sh`, `MAX_PER_SUITE.core` raised 146 -> 150 to stay at the P0 <=10-binary cap) and `tests/support/lanecov.rs`'s `UNROUTED_ALLOWLIST` entries for the fixture paths (non-`.rs` files with no matching lane glob).
non_goals: No server-side compilation of source to Wasm -- the agent brings a component; a compile service is its own product decision.
No Python-in-Wasm -- component tooling for Python is still immature (the reason this PRD was held); the python kind remains for Python source, unmodified.
No change to the python kind or its sandbox -- `src/kinds/python.rs`, `src/sandbox.rs` untouched.

No WASI sockets/HTTP from inside the component in this slice -- pure compute + stdin/stdout-style I/O through call arguments and the result; outbound calls stay the http kind's job. (A conforming guest still links wasi:cli/clocks/random via the Rust std allocator's own abort path -- denied at the `WasiCtx` policy level: no preopened directories, no inherited network -- not by refusing WASI as a whole.)

No per-plan component size cap -- the PRD's own Open Questions table left 'component size cap per plan (free vs pro)' to be decided 'at build'; this slice ships one global cap (47 KiB / 48128 bytes, sized to clear the oom fixture's WASI-linked footprint with margin under the 64 KiB global spec-size cap after base64 overhead) since no other kind's binary/size limits vary per plan today either -- per-plan differentiation is left to a follow-on PRD.

No P2 requirement 9 (corpus-task proposal via the promote-usecase path) -- the PRD's own ten acceptance criteria stop at AC10, none of which cover it; left out of this build's scope rather than attempted without a corresponding proof.

additional.no_server_side_compile: The wasm kind accepts only an already-compiled component (base64 in the spec, the same transport python's `source` field already uses for text); mcphost never invokes a Wasm toolchain itself.
additional.no_os_sandbox_dependency: The wasm execution path never invokes bwrap, unshare, or any external sandbox binary -- isolation is Wasmtime's own fuel/StoreLimits/epoch-interruption, proven independent of `sandbox_mechanism`'s own readiness by AC4.
additional.component_model_validation_at_publish: A core-module-only binary (no component-model wrapper) is rejected at publish with a structured error naming 'component model' as the requirement, via `wasmtime::component::Component::new`'s own parse failure -- not a hand-rolled binary-format sniff.
additional.wasmtime_pinned_version: wasmtime/wasmtime-wasi pinned to 38.0.4 (not a floating range), recorded verbatim in `/healthz`'s `wasm_runtime_version` field, matching this crate's other embedded-runtime dependency conventions.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did 45 of 45 python publishes fail on the hub on 2026-09-04?
five_whys_trace.a: Ubuntu's apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns broke bwrap, the OS-level primitive the python kind's sandbox depends on -- an entire capability went dead in production while /healthz kept reporting the sandbox as fine (vision, cycle 53).

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a single distro policy change take down an entire tool kind?
five_whys_trace.a: The python kind's isolation is a property of the host box's OS configuration (userns/AppArmor), not of mcphost itself -- the fix (an AppArmor profile) has to be carried to every box by the deploy tool, and until it is, the kind is simply unavailable.

five_whys_trace.q: Why not just fix cycle 53's specific AppArmor gap and move on?
five_whys_trace.a: That fixes this one incident but not the underlying dependency: any future distro/kernel change to unprivileged userns semantics can break bwrap again. Separately, per-tenant virtualenvs mean N× disk/build time and a real warm-up cost on first call after publish -- a second, independent cost cycle 53 didn't even touch.

five_whys_trace.q: Why hasn't a kind whose isolation doesn't depend on host OS policy shipped already?
five_whys_trace.a: Component-tooling for compiled sandboxed execution was immature until recently; the vision held a Wasm runtime as the python kind's principled successor since the first fleet (2026-09-02) but WASI 0.3 with async I/O only shipped in production-supportable form in February 2026, and Wasmtime being a pure Rust library (no subprocess, no host sandbox dependency) is what makes 'isolation travels with the binary' actually true rather than aspirational.

five_whys_trace.q: Why ship this now, as a narrow additive slice, rather than a broader Wasm story (server-side compile, WASI sockets/HTTP, Python-in-Wasm)?
five_whys_trace.a: The landscape now supports the narrow slice (component-model validation, fuel/memory/epoch limits, an embedded runtime) without those larger, riskier pieces; Joe pulled this held component forward on 2026-09-12 specifically because the operational cost of cycle 53 (an entire kind dead in production from one OS policy change) is a proven, recurring risk class the narrow slice already eliminates, while server-side compilation and Python-in-Wasm remain separate product decisions with their own tooling-maturity gates.

On the size-cap open question: this slice ships one global component-size cap (47 KiB / 48128 bytes) rather than a per-plan one -- sized empirically so the largest real fixture (the oom guest, which unavoidably links the full wasi:cli world via the Rust std allocator's abort path even though the guest code itself never touches sockets/filesystem) clears it with margin, while a spec at just over the bound still stays under the pre-existing global 64 KiB spec-storage cap once base64-encoded, so AC2's 'refused with a structured error naming the bound' proof doesn't collide with a second, unrelated cap. No other kind in this codebase varies its own size/resource limits per plan today, so introducing that axis only for wasm was judged out of scope for this slice and left to a follow-on PRD (recorded in non_goals) rather than guessed at without a plans.toml precedent to follow. Requirement 9 (P2, a corpus-task proposal) has no corresponding entry in the PRD's own ten-item Acceptance criteria list, so it was left out of this build's scope entirely rather than attempted without a proof to satisfy -- consistent with every other PRD-specific ambiguity resolution in this card's history choosing the PRD's own AC list as the actual contract, not the fuller Requirements table.
